requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's lan-a address for hosts on lan-a
requirements.summary: node1's PowerDNS recursor was configured with a static-host-mapping for app.internal -> 10.50.10.12 (node3's lan-a IP) and bound to the lan-a interface (10.50.10.1). node3, configured to use node1 as its DNS server, successfully resolved app.internal to 10.50.10.12 via getent and pinged it successfully. The same resolution and reachability were re-verified after node1 and node3 were independently rebooted, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's lan-b address for hosts on lan-b
requirements.summary: After an initial misconfigured attempt via dnsmasq's config.xml structure, the executor added an Unbound host override (app.internal -> 10.50.20.12, node4's lan-b IP) and reconfigured Unbound, which listens on port 53 on the lan-b (opt1) interface. A raw DNS query to 10.50.20.254:53 returned 10.50.20.12. node4, configured to use node2 as DNS, resolved app.internal via getent and pinged it successfully. Resolution and reachability were re-verified after node2 and node4 were independently rebooted.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — node1 resolving app.internal to node3's lan-a address for lan-a hosts, and node2 resolving app.internal to node4's lan-b address for lan-b hosts — are directly demonstrated as satisfied, including successful resolution and ping tests from the lan-a/lan-b hosts, and the same behavior re-verified after independently rebooting all four nodes (satisfying the provider-wide restart evidence protocol with clear pre/post boot-identity transitions and recovered DNS behavior on every node). The executor experimented with an incorrect approach on OPNsense (dnsmasq) before settling on Unbound, leaving an unused dnsmasq host entry and a few scratch scripts on node2 that were not cleaned up; a separate interface-addressing mistake on node1 was corrected within the same session.
limitations: The executor's own final report and selected evidence list were placeholder/test values ('test', cmd-1) and did not reference real command IDs; this evaluation relies entirely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots rather than the executor's self-reported summary.

It cannot be fully confirmed from the captured evidence whether the leftover dnsmasq 'hosts' entry on node2 causes any conflict with Unbound, since only unbound (port 53) was tested as the client-facing resolver; the dnsmasq entry appears unused but was not verified to be entirely inert.

The scratch Python scripts left in /tmp on node2 were not confirmed via the temporary-files diff (which shows only auto-generated tmpcfd_* churn), so their persistence at task end is inferred from the absence of any removal command, not directly observed in the final snapshot.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were tied to satisfying the DNS requirement or to necessary prerequisites (interface addressing, client resolver configuration) or to the provider-wide restart protocol. However, several unnecessary/residual mutations occurred on node2 (OPNsense): (1) an initial dnsmasq 'hosts' entry for app.internal was added directly via a base64-decoded Python script editing config.xml (cmd-abbbacf02baf4ac4) and corrected with a second script (cmd-49b3dd72f3454159), but this dnsmasq host entry was never removed even though the final working solution used Unbound instead, leaving an unused/duplicate DNS host mapping in the configuration; (2) three scratch Python scripts (/tmp/opnsense_dns.py, /tmp/fix_hosts.py, /tmp/add_unbound_host.py) were left on node2's filesystem with no cleanup command observed. On node1, an initial incorrect interface-address assignment (eth1=10.50.10.254, eth2=10.50.99.1, cmd-3baf0cb536614fa8) was promptly corrected in a later commit (cmd-1e0e187b827e4bda), a bounded and fully-reverted mutation. Several other actions (configctl interface newif/reload, tcpdump start) failed without changing state and are not penalized.
